# Our Practice

[Request Appointment](https://looppt.com/physical-therapist-appointment/)

Loop Physical Therapy provides a unique quality of care in many aspects of health care. We have a highly experienced team of physical therapists in [Edgewater](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/edgewater-il/), [The Chicago Loop](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/the-loop-chicago-il/), [West Loop Chicago, IL](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/west-loop-chicago-il/), [Terrace Clinic](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/oakbrook-terrace-il/) and [Barrington, IL](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/barrington-il/) that care for our patient’s physical wellness and provide home services to those who are in need. We also specialize in nutritional wellness, early diabetes prevention, and acupuncture. Our patients have found high levels of success in our treatment services, due to our implementation of advanced technology and methods.

We use sophisticated diagnostic methods, such as movement investigation and gait analysis, to help determine which services you will benefit from most. At Loop Physical Therapy, our thorough evaluations lead to successful treatment plans for your pain relief, healing, and future injury prevention needs.

## Our goal is to meet and exceed the expectations of our patients!

![Our Practice](https://looppt.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/DSC00497-copy-scaled-1.jpg)

![Our Practice](https://looppt.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/DSC00298-scaled-1.jpg)

At Loop Physical Therapy, we have one mission: helping you reach your highest physical potential. Our treatment plans are aimed toward the achievement of your goals, taking into account your symptoms, medical history, and any health restrictions you may have. We look forward to watching you achieve your recovery, health and fitness goals! With our care and commitment, we know that is possible for anyone who walks through our doors.

If you are in the Chicago area, or any of the surrounding areas, and you are looking for relief, look no further. Loop Physical Therapy is here to help as one of the most favored physical therapy practices in [Edgewater](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/edgewater-il/), [The Chicago Loop](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/the-loop-chicago-il/), [West Loop Chicago, IL](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/west-loop-chicago-il/), [Terrace Clinic](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/oakbrook-terrace-il/) and [Barrington, IL](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/barrington-il/). Call our office at [(773) 541-2020](tel:7735412020) to [request an appointment](https://looppt.com/physical-therapist-appointment/) with one of our physical therapists today! We will be happy to meet with you and create a plan for your journey toward health, healing, and pain relief.

At the end of the day, the Loop Physical Therapy team is here to provide support to you – the patient. Our success is dependent upon your success, and we strive to create a warm, welcoming environment where you can comfortably heal.

# Back Pain Relief

[Request Appointment](https://looppt.com/physical-therapist-appointment/)

## How Can Someone With Back Pain Benefit From Physical Therapy?

Are you relentlessly pursuing relief from back pain? Are you tired of remedies that promise a lot but deliver a little? Your quest for comfort ends here!

People with back pain are often trapped in a cycle of discomfort, restricted movement, and anxiety about their condition. However, hope is not lost. Physical therapy at Loop Physical Therapy offers a powerful pathway to alleviate this suffering, restoring mobility and quality of life.

Back pain is a pervasive problem, impacting millions of lives daily. It’s estimated that approximately 80% of the population will experience back pain at some point in their lives. Furthermore, low back pain is the most common cause of job-related disability.

Although back pain affects individuals across all age spectrums, it is most common among adults aged 35 to 55 years. The intensity of pain can range from a dull, constant ache to a sudden, sharp sensation that leaves the person incapacitated. While most cases of back pain are acute, lasting for a few days to weeks, some individuals may experience chronic back pain, which persists for 12 weeks or longer, even after an initial injury or underlying cause of acute low back pain has been treated.

Our physical therapy approach in [Edgewater](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/edgewater-il/), [The Chicago Loop](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/the-loop-chicago-il/), [West Loop Chicago, IL](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/west-loop-chicago-il/), [Terrace Clinic](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/oakbrook-terrace-il/) and [Barrington, IL](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/barrington-il/) has been shown to reduce back pain significantly. We can substantially improve your pain levels and functional abilities by focusing on strength and mobility exercises, posture correction, and education on protecting your back.

At Loop Physical Therapy, we understand that back pain is more than just discomfort—it impacts your ability to live, work, and enjoy life. We’re committed to providing tailored, evidence-based physical therapy solutions that address your unique needs.

**_Don’t let back pain dictate your life. [Contact us today and take your first step towards a pain-free future!](https://looppt.com/physical-therapist-appointment/)_**

[Get Started Today!](https://looppt.com/physical-therapist-appointment/)

## Why Does My Back Hurt?

Approximately 80% of adults experience back pain each year, making it one of the most prevalent health complaints worldwide. The intricate complexity of our back, consisting of a network of muscles, bones, ligaments, and nerves, often leaves us asking: “Why does my back hurt?” The answer to this question is multifaceted and hinges on a range of factors, from lifestyle choices and physical strain to underlying medical conditions.

Numerous research studies have linked back pain to several common culprits. Physical strain from activities such as heavy lifting or prolonged periods of sitting can lead to acute back pain. Additionally, lifestyle factors such as obesity, poor posture, and lack of physical activity can increase the risk of chronic back pain. Conditions like osteoarthritis and disc degeneration can also contribute to persistent pain.

Understanding the root cause of your back pain is just the beginning. A comprehensive and individualized treatment approach is crucial for alleviating pain and improving function. Physical therapy at Loop Physical Therapy is integral to this process. Through a combination of therapeutic exercises, manual therapy techniques, and patient education, physical therapists help patients manage their pain, enhance mobility, and prevent further injury.

The first step in your journey towards a pain-free life is understanding the ‘why’ behind your back pain. This knowledge enables you to make informed decisions about your treatment options and overall health.

**_[Reach out to us to schedule your first physical therapy session, and let our experienced team guide you on your path to recovery!](https://looppt.com/physical-therapist-appointment/)_**

[Request Appointment](https://looppt.com/physical-therapist-appointment/)

![Back-pain-relief-Loop-PT-Chicago-IL](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20500%20500'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## How Physical Therapy Can Provide Back Pain Relief

Physical therapy at Loop Physical Therapy is highly effective for relieving back pain. Our team of skilled physical therapists uses a combination of treatments validated by peer-reviewed research studies to address your unique needs and enhance your quality of life.

When you come in for an evaluation, our physical therapists first take a thorough history to understand your past illnesses, surgeries, and injuries. Next, we’ll conduct a hands-on assessment to assess the condition of your muscles and joints. This allows us to identify areas of tenderness or restrictions contributing to your back pain.

[Our physical therapists in](https://looppt.com/our-team/) [Edgewater](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/edgewater-il/), [The Chicago Loop](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/the-loop-chicago-il/), [West Loop Chicago, IL](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/west-loop-chicago-il/), [Terrace Clinic](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/oakbrook-terrace-il/) and [Barrington, IL](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/barrington-il/) will also perform specialized functional testing to understand how your back pain affects your everyday life and help us tailor our treatment plan to your specific needs and lifestyle.

We’ll utilize a range of treatment techniques, including the following:

- [Manual Therapy](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-treatments/manual-therapy/): This is a specialized form of physical therapy where our therapist uses his or her hands to apply pressure on muscle tissue and manipulate joints, aiming to decrease back pain caused by muscle spasms, tension, and joint dysfunction.
- [Therapeutic Exercise Programs](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-treatments/therapeutic-exercise/): Our therapists will design individualized exercise programs that can help improve strength, flexibility, mobility, and posture. Postural exercises can be used to correct alignment issues that may be contributing to pain.
- Pain Neuroscience Education (PNE): This approach aims to educate patients about pain and change beliefs and perceptions. Understanding the complex nature of pain can help reduce fear, misconceptions, and avoidance behaviors, which can help you resolve your pain once and for all!.
- Patient Education and Self-Management: This could involve learning about safe movement and lifting techniques, strategies for maintaining activity levels during a pain episode, methods for stress management, and understanding the warning signs of a potential back pain flare-up.
- [Shockwave Therapy](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-treatments/shockwave-therapy/): Acoustic waves with high energy peak used in Shockwave therapy interact with tissue causing accelerated tissue repair and cell growth, analgesia, and mobility restoration.

_**[Schedule a comprehensive evaluation with one of our expert physical therapists at Loop Physical Therapy!](https://looppt.com/physical-therapist-appointment/)**_

### Your Next Steps…

1. Request An Appointment

2. Receive A Custom Treatment Plan

3. Work Hard and Progress In Your Recovery

4. Recover & Enjoy Life Pain-Free!

Are you suffering from a persistent pain that’s limiting your physical abilities? If so, our physical therapy treatments can help you find relief, even if you have tried physical therapy before.

Pain doesn’t always work in traditional ways. Sometimes it can linger for days, weeks, or even months due to an underlying condition. ## How did my chronic pain develop?

In most cases, chronic pain stems from a neurophysiological origin. Chronic injury, illness, anxiety, and feeling depressed are intertwined in a complicated web, which leads your neurological system to always be on high alert. Chronic pain can appear in the form of back pain, joint pain, nerve pain, or headaches. It most commonly occurs due to one of the following causes:

- **Accidents –** Any accident can lead to chronic pain, whether it occurs in an automobile, workplace, or even in your own home. According to a 2016 statistic found by OSHA, workplace injuries happen to approximately 2.9 out of every 100 employees. Additionally, a study published in a journal called Pain determined that 21% of people involved in motor vehicle accidents develop chronic widespread pain in the weeks following their accident. This pain does not go away on its own, but seeking the help of a [Edgewater Chicago](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/loop-physical-therapy-edgewater/), [The Loop Chicago](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/lasalle-st-location/), [West Loop Chicago](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/physical-therapy-centers-chicago/) and [OakBrook Terrace, IL](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-clinic/terrace-satellite-clinic/) [physical therapist](https://looppt.com/physical-therapy-treatments/physical-therapy/) can help alleviate it.
- **Overuse Injuries –** Overuse injuries are very common, and they can occur in any part of the body that is used repetitively in your day-to-day life. For example, the way you stand, walk, work, and exercise can all take a toll on your body. It results in overuse injuries if you are not using proper techniques. This can result in damage to your joints and muscles, thus causing chronic pain. For example, if you perform heavy lifting at work many times a day, with improper techniques, this can lead to chronic back pain. Physical therapy can help you learn how to properly move your body in your everyday life, in order to avoid these issues.
- **Disease –** There are many diseases that can lead to chronic pain, including arthritis, fibromyalgia, multiple sclerosis, shingles, neuropathy as a result of diabetes, and more. These can all result in chronic pain, which can be alleviated through physical therapy treatments.
- **Surgery –** Surgical procedures are sometimes unavoidable. While they may be necessary for alleviating certain conditions you are facing, the post-surgical recovery period can be just as painful. Surgical repair of an area of the body is enough to correct a structural problem, but we often compensate in our movement for the pain we experience. Weeks, months, or even years of compensatory movement often causes additional pain after surgery if the movement is not corrected. Physical therapy offers post-surgical rehabilitation services that can help speed up recovery time, relieve pain, and reduce the risk of chronic pain in the future.

## What’s the difference between chronic and acute pain?

Acute pain can be defined as pain that goes away on its own in a few hours, days, or weeks. The example of a minor ankle sprain would be considered acute pain, as the pain will subside shortly within a few days.

Chronic pain is a constant discomfort that lasts for 3-6 months or longer. There are several reasons why people may experience chronic pain, and it is the most common reason for seeking medical help. It can greatly hinder your quality of life by limiting your mobility, creating a dependence on prescription drugs, or even causing anxiety and depression. Some people feel dizzy because they didn’t get enough sleep, ate poorly, did too much exercise, or have an illness like a head cold or the flu. Even things like alcohol or certain medicines can make you feel dizzy.

Some things happening in your body, like orthostatic hypotension (which occurs when you stand up too fast after lying or sitting for a long time), or issues with your eyes or migraines, can also cause dizziness.

- Feeling like you’re going to faint
- Seeing things like you’re looking through a tunnel
- Feeling heavy-headed or light-headed
- Feeling like you might throw up
- Not being steady on your feet

- Making your balance better: One common reason for dizziness is something in your inner ear called Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). We can help with special head and body movements that put things back in place and stop you from feeling dizzy.
- Doing balance exercises and exercises that help your brain and nerves work better, so you don’t feel as dizzy.
- Checking other things in your body, like your eyes and ears, and sometimes, we’ll ask other doctors like heart doctors to make sure there are no big problems. We’ll also look at your medicine to make sure it’s safe for you.

There are a number of reasons why neck pain may occur. When you experience neck pain, it typically can run from the base of your skull to the top of your shoulder blades, finally settling in the back of the neck. The pain may vary in severity, from a constant dull ache to sharp and stabbing pains. Neck pain can sometimes include additional symptoms, including but not limited to:

- Stiffness and muscle tightness in the upper body
- Numbness or tingling into the upper extremities
- Headaches
- Discomfort and pain when remaining in the same position for too long
- Arm weakness
- Loss of sleep due to pain and discomfort
- Inability to fully stand up or sit up straight

### Common conditions causing neck pain:

Neck pain is most commonly caused by an injury to the tissues or bone structures in the neck; however, certain degenerative conditions can also lead to neck pain. Some common conditions that give you a pain in your neck include:

###### Injuries

Whiplash, typically sustained by an automobile or high-impact sports collision, is one of the most common injuries that results in neck pain. This is known as a “strain” injury, causing the head to whip rapidly back-and-forth, thus affecting the soft tissues in the back of the neck.

###### Illnesses

Certain diseases and ailments can result in neck pain, such as rheumatoid arthritis, meningitis, or cancer.

###### Nerve compression

If you have a herniated disc in your neck, or narrowing of the foramen (space where the nerves exit the spine), the nerves that branch out from your spinal cord can become compressed. In some cases, nerve pain can even extend from the neck all the way down to the hands and fingers — a condition known as “radiculopathy.”

###### Muscle strains

The muscles in your neck can become strained by overuse. Even something as simple as sitting at your desk all day with your neck craned toward the computer screen can lead to a strain in your neck muscles.

###### Joint degeneration

Much like any other joint in your body, the neck joints can erode with age, causing pain. Conditions such as osteoarthritis can also reduce the cartilage between the vertebrae in the neck, also resulting in neck pain.

Next, they perform a meticulous hands-on assessment. This hands-on evaluation helps tailor a therapy plan that is customizable to your needs. Our therapists will assess the flexibility and power of your foot and ankle, identifying any limitations or weaknesses. This vital information guides the development of an effective treatment strategy that targets these identified areas.

We offer a variety of research-supported treatments for foot pain, including:

  • Therapeutic Exercises: Specific exercises are customized to enhance mobility, boost strength, and restore function in your foot. These could include stretching, strengthening, and balance activities.
  • Manual Therapy: Using their hands, therapists manipulate the foot to improve mobility, reduce pain, and stimulate healing. Techniques include joint and soft tissue mobilization and massage.
  • Gait Training: Gait training involves retraining patients on how to walk safely and efficiently to improve mobility. After a foot injury or condition, the natural way of walking may be altered due to pain or decreased function.
  • Balance and Coordination Activities: These exercises are designed to improve the patient’s proprioception – the body’s ability to sense its location, movements, and actions.

Educating patients is a crucial part of physical therapy. We’ll provide knowledge and tools to help patients understand their conditions, manage pain, and prevent future injuries.
